faq.q: Which is bigger, the Mangusta 80 or Sunseeker Predator 74?
faq.a: The Mangusta 80 is 24m long, while the Sunseeker Predator 74 is 22.5m. The Mangusta also offers a larger flybridge and sun deck, making it better for groups who want to spread out. Both can carry 12 passengers, but the Mangusta’s layout feels more spacious.

faq.q: Does the Sunseeker Predator 74 come with a jet ski?
faq.a: No. Only our Mangusta 80 (white or grey) includes a free jet ski on charter. The Sunseeker Predator 74 is not in our fleet, but we recommend the Mangusta 80 for the added water toy and better value at €4,719 for 4 hours.

faq.q: Can I charter a Sunseeker Predator 74 in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, other operators offer Sunseeker Predator 74 charters, but we do not. Our fleet focuses on boats like the Mangusta 80, Azimut 58, and Ferretti 94. For a similar sporty feel, consider the Pershing 46 or Azimut 39.

faq.q: What is the price difference between the Mangusta 80 and Sunseeker Predator 74?
faq.a: Our Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours (skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, jet ski included). A Sunseeker Predator 74 typically costs €4,500–€6,000 for 4 hours, but without a jet ski. The Mangusta offers better value for groups.

faq.q: Which boat is better for a party in Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Both can handle parties, but the Mangusta 80 has a larger flybridge and aft deck, perfect for dancing or lounging. The Sunseeker Predator 74 is more streamlined and sporty, better for a small group wanting speed. For 12 guests, the Mangusta wins.

faq.q: Are both boats suitable for families with children?
faq.a: Yes, both are safe for families. The Mangusta 80 has more shaded areas and a stable ride, plus the jet ski is a hit with older kids. We recommend the Mangusta 80 for family charters due to its extra space and amenities.

faq.q: Where do the Mangusta 80 and Sunseeker Predator 74 depart from?
faq.a: Our Mangusta 80 departs from Puerto Banús, Marbella. The Sunseeker Predator 74, if chartered elsewhere, often departs from Marbella Marina or Sotogrande. Puerto Banús offers easy access to Cala del Faro and Cabopino.

faq.q: What is the top speed of the Mangusta 80 vs Sunseeker Predator 74?
faq.a: The Mangusta 80 cruises at 24–28 knots (top ~32 knots). The Sunseeker Predator 74 is slightly faster at 30–34 knots, due to its lighter build. For leisurely cruising and anchoring, both are excellent.

data.body_html:
Choosing between a Mangusta 80 vs Sunseeker Predator 74 for your Marbella charter? Both are stunning 24-metre-class yachts, but they serve different vibes. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) departs Puerto Banús and includes a free jet ski from €4,719 for 4 hours. The Sunseeker Predator 74 (22.5m, 12 pax) is sportier but not in our fleet. This comparison covers specs, price, space, and the best pick for your day on the Costa del Sol. For our full fleet, see [Boat Rental Marbella](/).

Mangusta 80 vs Sunseeker Predator 74: Key Specs

SpecMangusta 80Sunseeker Predator 74
Length24m22.5m
Beam5.6m5.1m
Passengers1212
Cabins44
Top speed~32 knots~34 knots
Jet ski includedYes (free)No
Starting price (4h)€4,719~€4,500–€6,000

The Mangusta 80 is slightly longer and beamier, giving more deck space. The Predator 74 is marginally faster but less roomy for socialising.

Price & Value: Mangusta 80 Wins on Inclusions

Our Mangusta 80 (Tier B) costs €4,719 minimum 4 hours, with a free jet ski, licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish VAT. The Sunseeker Predator 74, if chartered elsewhere, often costs similar or more but without a jet ski. For a group of 12, the Mangusta delivers better value—especially if you want to wakeboard, tube, or explore coves.

All our charters depart from Puerto Banús, so you can head straight to Cala Cortés or Cabopino without extra fees.

Space & Layout: Mangusta 80 Has More Social Zones

The Mangusta 80 features a large flybridge with sun pads, a spacious aft deck with dining, and a generous bow sunbathing area. The Sunseeker Predator 74 is more streamlined—its cockpit is smaller, and the flybridge is less expansive. For a party, family gathering, or corporate event, the Mangusta 80 lets guests spread out comfortably.

If you prefer a sporty, low-profile look, the Predator 74 might appeal, but for practical chartering, the Mangusta’s layout is superior.

Performance: Sunseeker Faster, Mangusta Smoother

The Sunseeker Predator 74 can hit 34 knots thanks to its lighter construction and more powerful engines. The Mangusta 80 cruises at 24–28 knots and tops out around 32 knots. However, the Mangusta’s deeper V-hull provides a more stable ride in Mediterranean chop. For leisurely cruising along the Golden Mile or anchoring off Estepona, both are excellent, but the Mangusta feels more planted.

Which Boat Is Best for Your Marbella Charter?

Choose the Mangusta 80 if you want:

  • Maximum deck space for 12 guests
  • A free jet ski for water sports
  • All-inclusive pricing with no hidden extras
  • Departure from Puerto Banús

Consider the Sunseeker Predator 74 if you:

  • Prefer a sportier, more aggressive design
  • Want slightly higher top speed
  • Are okay with less deck space and no jet ski

For most groups, the Mangusta 80 is the better charter choice. If you need a smaller boat, see our Azimut 39 or Astondoa 40.

Where to Go on a Mangusta 80 Charter

From Puerto Banús, popular routes include:

  • Cala Cortés – 20 min, turquoise water, cliff jumping
  • Cabopino – 30 min, sandy beach, chiringuitos
  • Estepona – 45 min, old town, seafood
  • Sotogrande – 1 hour, luxury marina, golf

With the free jet ski, you can also explore Cala del Faro or tow a friend on a tube. All safety equipment is included.
